$comment: Transcription capability registry — the machine-readable capability boundary for filing-transcription-spec.md §6. The workbook check reads this file: 'unsupported' constructs fail with `message` (R-190); 'partial' constructs pass with `message` as a warning (R-191). Statuses move unsupported → partial → supported as the platform grows; the spec text does not change. Versioned independently of the spec.

constructs.label: Additive endorsements on multi-coverage plans
constructs.detected_by: endorsements: kind=additive (or rate_branch) when plan.coverages has more than one entry
constructs.message: A filed additive endorsement applies ONCE per policy; with multiple coverage towers the engine has no single tip to attach it to (package-level endorsement layering is pending). The projector refuses rather than applying it N times.
constructs.instead: Factor endorsements work on any plan (distributive). For a once-per-policy amount on a multi-coverage plan, record it in gaps_and_assumptions until package-level layering ships.

constructs.label: Constant (unkeyed) factors as chain stages
constructs.message: The engine cannot key a constant chain factor, so the projector refuses it instead of silently changing premium.
constructs.instead: Express it as a 1-D factor table over a declared dimension (a two-level yes/no dimension for conditional factors like sprinkler credits), or as a loading when it applies post-tower.

constructs.label: Non-equality predicate operators on chain stages and loadings
constructs.message: The platform's factor gate (FactorPredicate) tests equality only — a chain or loading predicate using != < <= > >= in not-in cannot be expressed, and the builder refuses rather than mis-gating a factor.
constructs.instead: Express a threshold or set condition as a 1-D factor table over a banded (or yes/no categorical) dimension of the same input, with factor 1.0 on the levels where it doesn't apply; or record the condition in gaps_and_assumptions. == predicates work everywhere; endorsements.trigger executes the full §4.6.1 grammar.

constructs.label: Per-coverage rounding in final adjustments (round each tower, then sum)
constructs.detected_by: final_adjustments: kind=round with non-empty applies_to, or more than one round row
constructs.message: The engine's round stage is the plan-tail total-rounder: it sums the per-coverage premiums, floors, and rounds ONCE at the package level. Rounding each coverage before summing is not expressible.
constructs.instead: Author one package-level round row. Filed per-coverage premiums stay in test_cases with tolerance_<field> = 0.5 (they differ from the unrounded tower outputs by cents); record the source's per-coverage rounding in gaps_and_assumptions. Per-coverage CLAMPS (minimum premiums) still work.

constructs.label: Linear interpolation between factor-table breakpoints
constructs.message: A table flagged `interpolation=linear` interpolates — a 2-D table along its flagged banded axis (lookup.multi interpolateOn), or a 1-D banded curve through the engine's interpolate kind. Breakpoints anchor at band LOWER bounds, ends clamp, and on-anchor values are byte-exact. Unflagged tables step. R-111 is a notice naming each interpolating table.

constructs.label: Multi-location policies (one insured, N rated locations)
constructs.detected_by: not detectable in the workbook; policy-level concern
constructs.message: The platform rates one risk unit per row and aggregates locations at the policy scoring seam. Location-level rating transcribes normally; policy-level combination rules beyond summation are not expressible.
constructs.instead: Transcribe the per-location algorithm; record policy-level combination rules (per-policy minimums across locations, location interdependencies) in gaps_and_assumptions.

constructs.label: Per-vehicle / per-driver rating with assignment algorithms (auto)
constructs.message: The platform rates one risk unit per row; driver-to-vehicle assignment algorithms cannot be expressed.
constructs.instead: Where the book allows, decompose to one row per vehicle and record the assignment rule in gaps_and_assumptions (kind=unsupported).

constructs.label: Cross-product packages (multiple products on one policy, package credits across them)
constructs.detected_by: one workbook = one product (plan.product is scalar)
constructs.message: One product per workbook/plan. Package interactions across products have no home.
constructs.instead: One workbook per product; record cross-product credits/interactions in gaps_and_assumptions.

constructs.label: Arbitrary DAG topologies (fan-out, diamond joins, a factor consumed by two stages)
constructs.detected_by: the chains sheet expresses linear towers only
constructs.message: The workbook expresses a linear tower per coverage; arbitrary wiring is not expressible.
constructs.instead: Most filed manuals are linear towers. Anything else: record in gaps_and_assumptions; hand-wire post-ingest if truly needed.

constructs.label: N-way conditional branching (case/branch logic)
constructs.message: Simple conditions ride `predicate` columns; true N-way branching has no tabular form.
constructs.instead: Express two-way conditions as predicated stages/tables; record genuine branching in gaps_and_assumptions.

constructs.label: Free-form formula stages (computed intermediate values)
constructs.message: Derived values (ratios, formula factors) cannot be computed by the workbook; inputs arrive as data.
constructs.instead: Declare the derived quantity as an input (the dataset supplies it pre-computed) and record the derivation in gaps_and_assumptions; or express a filed formula as a banded table at the filing's breakpoints.

constructs.label: Sub-plan composition / stacked per-state amendments
constructs.message: Base-plus-overlay layering is not expressible; workbooks are self-contained.
constructs.instead: Flatten: transcribe the effective algorithm with citations pointing at both the base and the amendment (spec §7.3).

constructs.label: Model-backed factors (GLM/ML scores evaluated in-plan)
constructs.message: Filed tables only; models are not transcription artifacts.
constructs.instead: If the filing references a scoring model's OUTPUT, declare it as an input; record the model itself in gaps_and_assumptions.

constructs.label: Class-conditional exposure bases (different divisor per class)
constructs.detected_by: chains carry one exposure_divisor per stage
constructs.message: One exposure divisor per chain exposure stage.
constructs.instead: Split coverages/towers where the filing genuinely rates different exposure bases; otherwise record the exception in gaps_and_assumptions. A future derived_from div(…) grammar can provide a direct representation.

constructs.label: Externally computed indices (WC experience mod, credit tiers) consumed as inputs
constructs.message: Declare an inputs row; the plan consumes the value.

constructs.label: Premium capping vs prior term
constructs.message: Supported when prior premium is declared as an input.

constructs.label: The workbook's rating_plan_id becomes the built plan's id
constructs.message: The same workbook produces the same plan id on any machine. Building against a taken id refuses: identical bytes = ingest_already_built (409); different bytes = ingest_plan_id_taken (409) pointing at the re-ingest door — never a silent duplicate.

constructs.label: Platform-computed inputs (inputs.derived_from)
constructs.message: derived_from = sum(<input>,<input>,…) over ≥2 declared numeric non-derived inputs makes the input platform-computed: never row-supplied (required=false, no default — R-046), usable as a lookup axis only (R-047; the value exists inside the rating graph, not on the row). div(…) is recognized and named-deferred to class_conditional_exposure.

constructs.label: Coverage election (optional coverages skip, not withhold)
constructs.detected_by: plan: coverages entries with a trailing `?` (spec §4.1)
constructs.message: A coverage marked electable (`building?`) elects OUT on an EXPLICIT 0 exposure: its tower's nodes skip and it contributes $0 with a 'not elected' trace line. Absence still withholds — you can't tell 'didn't buy' from 'didn't fill in'. An explicit 0 on a REQUIRED coverage prices the arithmetic ($0 tower) and warns. R-048: at least one coverage stays required; an electable coverage needs an exposure stage.
